challenge.title: Verify it's you
challenge.sentence: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
challenge.keySentence: Use your security key or passkey to finish signing in.
challenge.codeHelp: 6 digits from the app you set up for this account
challenge.keyPrompt: Follow your browser's prompt to use your security key or passkey.
challenge.lost: Lost your phone or key? Use another second factor or one of your recovery codes. If you have neither, ask an Owner or Admin of your organization to contact XOS support, who confirm who you are before removing the factor.

policy.enrollSentence: {org} requires a second factor for your role. Set one up to continue.
policy.sessionEnded: {org} asks you to sign in again every {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}.
policy.idle: You were inactive longer than {org} allows, so you need to sign in again.
policy.signedOut: This session was signed out from another device. Sign in again to continue.

stepUp.title: Confirm it's you
stepUp.sentence: Confirm with your second factor to continue.
stepUp.enrollSentence: This action needs a second factor. Set up an authenticator app now and use it for actions like this one.

enroll.label: Name
enroll.labelHelp: So you can tell your factors apart, for example Work phone
enroll.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
enroll.qrAlt: QR code that sets up your authenticator app
enroll.showSecret: Can't scan? Show the setup key
enroll.done: Your authenticator app is set up.
enroll.keyDone: Your security key is set up.
enroll.recovery: Keep a second way in. Add a second authenticator app or a security key, so losing one device never locks you out.

factors.title: Two-step verification
factors.description: A second factor keeps your account safe if your password or email is exposed. You use it when you sign in, and Restricted exports and emergency access need it. Removing a factor asks for a code from the last 15 minutes.
factors.required: {org} requires a second factor for your role.
factors.removeSentence: You won't be asked for it when you sign in. If it is your only second factor, your account is protected by your password alone.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of a password. The passkey stays on your device and works only on this site, so it can't be phished.
passkeys.label: Name
passkeys.removeSentence: You won't be able to sign in with this passkey. Remove it from your device too, in its password settings.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.sentence: Enter your work email. You continue to your organization's sign-in page.

providers.title: Enterprise single sign-on and SCIM
providers.description: People sign in through your identity provider (SAML 2.0), and SCIM adds and removes them as your directory changes. Single sign-on and SCIM never make anyone an Owner.
providers.notInPlan: Single sign-on and SCIM are part of the Enterprise plan.
providers.none: No identity provider yet. XOS support connects your provider and gives you its provider ID.
providers.name: Name
providers.nameHelp: For example the name of your identity provider tenant
providers.providerIdHelp: The single sign-on provider ID XOS support gave you
providers.jit: Add people who sign in through this provider
providers.tokenOnce: Copy this token into your identity provider now. It is shown once; issuing another replaces it.
providers.domains: People whose verified domain is {domains} can sign in with single sign-on.

errors.code_invalid: That code didn't match. Enter the code your app shows now.
errors.code_expired: That took too long. Try again.
errors.step_up_required: Confirm it's you with your second factor first.
errors.factor_limit: You have the most second factors allowed. Remove one first.
errors.factor_name_taken: You already have a factor with that name. Choose another.
errors.passkey_failed: Your device didn't confirm it. Try again.
errors.cancelled: Canceled. Try again when you're ready.
errors.unsupported: This browser doesn't support security keys or passkeys.
errors.sso_unavailable: No single sign-on is set up for that email domain. Sign in another way, or ask your Admin.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute, then try again.
errors.integration_plan_feature: Single sign-on and SCIM need the Enterprise plan.
errors.sso_default_role_owner: Single sign-on never makes anyone an Owner. Choose another role.
errors.conflict: Another identity provider already uses that provider ID.
errors.recovery_invalid: That recovery code didn't match, or it was already used.
errors.recovery_rate_limited: Too many wrong codes. Wait 15 minutes, then try again.
errors.no_codes: You have no recovery codes to use. Use another second factor, or ask an Owner or Admin to contact XOS support.
errors.recovery_codes_need_factor: Set up an authenticator app or a security key first.
errors.session_current: To sign out of this device, use Sign out.
errors.oauth_request_expired: This sign-in request has expired. Go back to the app and start again.
errors.oauth_request_recorded: This sign-in request was already started. Go back to the app and start again.
errors.oauth_client_unknown: This app isn't registered with XOS.
errors.oauth_not_member: Only members of the organization that registered this app can connect it.
errors.oauth_scope_unknown: This app asked for an area XOS doesn't have.
errors.oauth_scope_missing: This app didn't say which areas it needs.
errors.oauth_pkce_required: This app must use PKCE with S256. Ask its developer to update it.
errors.plan_feature_required: API keys need the Pro plan or above.
errors.api_key_expiry_invalid: Choose an expiry within a year.

recovery.title: Recovery codes
recovery.description: Single-use codes for when you can't use your authenticator app or security key. Keep them somewhere safe, away from your phone.
recovery.needFactor: Set up an authenticator app or a security key first. Recovery codes stand in for it.
recovery.noneLeft: You've used every code. Make a new set.
recovery.low: {remaining, plural, one {Only # code left.} other {Only # codes left.}} Make a new set soon.
recovery.regenerateSentence: Your current codes stop working as soon as the new ones are made.
recovery.shownOnce: Save these codes now. You won't see them again, and each one works once.
recovery.codeHelp: 10 letters and digits from your saved codes, like abcde-23456
recovery.used: Code accepted. {remaining, plural, =0 {You have no codes left. Make a new set in Security.} one {You have # code left.} other {You have # codes left.}}

sessions.title: Sessions and devices
sessions.description: Where you're signed in to Atlas, Gateway and Compass. Sign out of anything you don't recognize.
sessions.signOutSentence: That session ends now. Anyone using it has to sign in again.
sessions.signOutOthersTitle: Sign out of every other session?
sessions.signOutOthersSentence: Every session except this one ends now. Apps you connected stay connected; revoke them under Connected apps.
sessions.signedOutOthers: {count, plural, =0 {No other session was signed in.} one {Signed out of # other session.} other {Signed out of # other sessions.}}

connectedApps.title: Connected apps
connectedApps.description: Apps you let use XOS for you. Each one reaches only the organization that registered it and the areas you allowed.
connectedApps.revokeSentence: {app} loses access at once and has to ask you again.

consent.title: Allow {app} to use XOS?
consent.org: {app} was registered by {org}. It acts as you in {org} only, and only in the areas below.
consent.restrictedNote: Some of these reach Restricted data or control the organization. You'll confirm it's you with your second factor.
consent.redirect: After you choose, you go back to {uri}.
consent.expired: This request has expired, or it isn't yours. Go back to the app and start again.
consent.pkce: This app can't connect safely: it doesn't use PKCE with S256. Ask its developer to update it.
consent.invalid: This sign-in request is incomplete. Go back to the app and start again.

oauthApps.title: OAuth apps
oauthApps.description: Apps people in {org} can connect to their own account. They sign in with XOS and allow only the areas they see on the consent screen.
oauthApps.name: App name
oauthApps.redirectHelp: Where XOS sends people back: an https address, or a loopback address for a native app
oauthApps.pkce: A public client: no client secret. Apps use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and ask for areas in scope, for example "projects schedule".
oauthApps.removeSentence: Everyone who connected it loses access at once.
